details:
camelot-ammv2-periphery namesquats Camelot DEX's AMM v2 periphery contracts, published as a brand-new npm package with no relation to any real distribution under this name. Version 1.0.0 (published 2026-08-11 ~05:41-06:08 UTC) shipped a `preinstall`/`postinstall` hook (`node index.js || true`) that scans `process.env` for variable names matching a credential regex (KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASS, PRIVATE, MNEMONIC, RPC, AWS, GITHUB, NPM, KUBE, VAULT, AUTH, PGP, GPG, SEED, WALLET), reads `~/.npmrc` and `~/.gitconfig`, and lists `~/.ssh`, `~/.foundry/keystores`, `~/.config/hardhat`, and `~/.config/gcloud`, POSTing the harvested data to a webhook.site endpoint. The 1.0.0 payload's header comment falsely self-identified as `@plumenetwork/nest-artifacts`, an install-time shim for an unrelated project — a copy-paste artifact from whatever template the actor reused across this batch.

A 1.1.0 release published roughly 3 hours later (~09:00-09:01 UTC) meaningfully escalates the payload: the credential regex gained BEARER, API, INFURA, ALCHEMY, HELIUS, QUICKNODE, and ANKR (RPC/API provider key patterns); directory listings were replaced with full file-content reads (first ~4000 bytes) of `.aws/credentials`, `.aws/config`, `.ssh/id_rsa`, `.ssh/id_ed25519`, `.ssh/config`, `.kube/config`, `.docker/config.json`, `.netrc`, `.pgpass`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.gitconfig`, `.git-credentials`, and GCP application-default credentials; it now also reads local `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.production`, `.env.development`, and `secrets.env` from the install working directory; and it adds direct cryptocurrency wallet keystore theft — reading file contents (not just listing) from Solana (`.config/solana/id.json`, `.solana/id.json`), Anchor (`.config/anchor/id.json`), NEAR (`.near-credentials`), and Sui (`.sui/sui.keystore`) wallet paths, plus the contents (not just names) of the first three files in `~/.foundry/keystores`. The false `@plumenetwork/nest-artifacts` header comment was removed in 1.1.0. Both versions exfiltrate to the same webhook.site path over HTTPS POST, wrapped in a bare try/catch so failures never surface.

This package is one of six published from the same npm account (`mssjeep843`) namesquatting real DeFi protocols (Euler's EVC, Aerodrome Finance, Camelot AMM, and the boring-vault pattern), all sharing the same webhook.site callback path and the same 1.0.0-to-1.1.0 escalation pattern. Two further packages from the same actor and same webhook.site path (PyPI `dlmm` and `dlmm-sdk`, namesquatting Meteora's DLMM SDK) were also sandbox-confirmed running an equivalent harvester but have since been removed from PyPI; those are tracked separately as MAL-2026-13728 and MAL-2026-13729.

Any environment where either version was installed should be treated as having had its environment variables and any present SSH keys, cloud/Kubernetes/Docker credentials, `.env` files, and Solana/Anchor/NEAR/Sui/Foundry wallet keys exposed to the attacker; rotate all reachable secrets immediately, prioritizing wallet private keys and RPC/API provider tokens if 1.1.0 was installed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code

files.note: 1.1.0 escalated payload: adds wallet keystore theft (Solana/Anchor/NEAR/Sui), local .env file reads, expanded RPC/API key regex, full credential-file-content reads
